rv.q: The questions 'Race' poses and the answers its characters supply add up to an intriguing study of perception — from both black and white viewpoints.
This play will, I suspect, attract furious criticism from the left.
Mamet has fashioned a theatrical thriller that keeps you guessing about the motivations and machinations of everyone onstage.
But as it is, it's a lit fuse that crackles and pops but never quite explodes.

Race raises interesting questions, but doesn't ground them in characters that could bring their complications to life.
Audiences might expect this type of awkwardly constructed, flailing acrimony from a 15-year-old with a Twitter account, not from a Pulitzer Prize winner.
The more troubling question is whether, ultimately, we end up caring what he thinks in "Race," the attractively cast, surprisingly stale new play...
It's also a stunning return to original form for Mamet, who doesn't abandon the show-biz savvy of his middle period while jumping headfirst in the acidic repartee of his earlier, most defining works.
And Mamet deserves credit for a briskly entertaining, if flawed, study.
Luckily, these minor visual nuisances can be ignored, since Aukin hasn't neglected his central task: getting from his cast five uniformly affecting performances, rich, detailed, and sensibly unshowy.
There's no denying the production under Mamet's direction is plenty entertaining and thought provoking.
The shock is that the author elicits little more than a shrug once all the thrusts and parries, revelations and reversals are toted up.

cn.t: Mamet's provocative racial drama divides critics with its sharp dialogue and thorny questions about perception and prejudice, though some find it clunky and inconclusive rather than insightful.

vs.sum: The Ethel Barrymore Theatre offers good sightlines with a well-raked mezzanine and minimal obstructions, though some box seats have limited views. Sound quality is average, with some reports of less than ideal acoustics. Comfort is typical for a Broadway theater, with decent legroom in some areas. However, facilities are lacking, with only one restroom on the lower level leading to potential congestion.

acc.note: 5 wheelchair spaces in Orchestra. No steps from sidewalk. Infrared devices available.
